children: Shares in online brokerage FlatexDegiro fell after it said its chairman had stepped down from the role with immediate effect, and that another supervisory board member was leaving, due to differences of opinion about the company's strategic direction.
In European morning trade, shares were 5% lower at 32.56 euros, dragging their year-to-date performance to a 12% decline.
The company said late Thursday that Hans-Hermann Lotter had stepped down as chairman of the supervisory board with immediate effect, to be replaced by his deputy, Stefan Mueller, on an interim basis.
Lotter will also step down from the supervisory board no later than Oct. 10, when fellow board member Martina Pfeifer will also depart, it said.
The departures stem from differing views on the company's future strategic direction and positioning, FlatexDegiro said.
Lotter and Pfeifer were both elected to the board in June 2025 for a three-year term. FlatexDegiro said Lotter had guided the company through a period of strong growth and strategic development.
The company said its strategic and operational priorities remain unchanged, and backed its full-year guidance.
The board will immediately start looking for candidates to replace the pair, FlatexDegiro said.
